what_happened: On 2026-11-06 the person running Athena lifted the scope-guard pause on the producer build-slot line by hand, outside any job. The line's last attempt had passed checks, replay and verification. It went stale only because another change landed on main first. The pause had stopped it from being retried on the new base. The the person running Athena lifted the pause so the retry would resume the kept candidate and not repeat the spend. No acceptance criteria, findings or checks are listed.
cause: The scope guard counts spend on a line without asking why the attempt did not land. A verified attempt that went stale because main moved looks the same as spend that made no progress. Athena also has no way to carry verified work onto a new base (20261023-172306-erh5), so staleness shows up as a failed attempt. A person has to read the attempt's outcome, see that the candidate is kept and passed, and lift the pause. The guard has no rule for 'passed all gates, only the base changed'.
prevention: Make the scope guard count only spend from attempts that ended unverified or failed on their own merits. Spend from an attempt that passed checks, replay and verification and then went stale because the base moved is recorded as stale-base. It does not count toward a pause. The guard also shows a kept, verified candidate as waiting for a rebase retry. This applies to every line, not just the build-slot line. It needs a test with a verified-but-stale attempt that must not pause the line, and a test with a real no-progress attempt that must.
proposed_request: Change the scope guard so a line is not paused by spend from an attempt that passed checks, replay and verification and then went stale only because main moved. Record such an attempt as stale-base and keep its candidate for a resume-style retry. Acceptance: (1) a test where a verified attempt goes stale leaves the line unpaused and its spend out of the no-progress total; (2) a test where an attempt fails verification or produces nothing still counts toward the pause as before; (3) the status output lists the kept candidate as waiting to be retried on the new base. No config changes. Do not change how the guard treats low-disk or other environment stops.
